fig1_monthly_revenue.title: Figure 1. Monthly net merchandise revenue
fig1_monthly_revenue.caption: Peak months: November 2011 (GBP 1,119,164), November 2010 (GBP 1,117,670), October 2010 (GBP 976,736). Complete-month Q4/rest mean revenue ratio: 1.53. December 2011 ends 09 December 2011. Reversals are attributed to the original sale month.

fig2_products.title: Figure 2. Products ranked separately by each measure
fig2_products.caption: revenue leader: REGENCY CAKESTAND 3 TIER (22423), 261,233 GBP; units leader: WORLD WAR 2 GLIDERS ASSTD DESIGNS (84077), 103,697 units; customers leader: WHITE HANGING HEART T-LIGHT HOLDER (85123A), 1,484 customers. The leaders differ. Each row shows its customer count; full names are in product_summary.csv.

fig3_countries.title: Figure 3. Highest-revenue export countries (United Kingdom excluded)
fig3_countries.caption: EIRE leads exports: GBP 567,786, 3 customers. Netherlands has the largest AOV in this group: GBP 2,538.50, 1,774.2 units/order, 22 customers; UK: GBP 411.79, 247.3 units/order. Basket size and customer-base size are descriptive, not proof of buyer type.

fig4_cancellations.title: Figure 4. Cancellation invoices and invoice rate
fig4_cancellations.caption: Complete-month mean invoice cancellation rate: Q4 16.21%; non-Q4 17.03%. No descriptive Q4 elevation is observed. Both invoice counts use identified customers and merchandise codes; gross purchase invoices precede netting. Final month is partial.

feature_correlations.title: Customer feature Pearson correlations (raw scale)
feature_correlations.caption: AOV = Monetary / Frequency. Monetary-Frequency correlation: 0.624. Correlation is descriptive and does not establish causality.

fig5_transformations.title: Figure 5. Raw and log-transformed customer features
fig5_transformations.caption: Absolute skew decreases for Recency, Frequency, Monetary, AOV, Variety, CancellationRate. CancellationRate is zero for 58.8% of customers; skew 1.32 to 1.14. Histograms include outliers; model fitting excludes the upper log-Monetary fence.

fig6_selection.title: Figure 6. Feature-set and cluster-count comparison
fig6_selection.caption: Selected rfm, k=2 by highest silhouette 0.438; Davies-Bouldin 0.873; mean pairwise seed ARI 0.999. Metrics describe this sample; they do not prove future usefulness.

fig7_pca.title: Figure 7. PCA view of fitted customers
fig7_pca.caption: PCA displays 94.8% of transformed feature variance. Colours are pipeline predictions. Projection overlap is not a separate clustering evaluation; outliers were excluded from fitting.

fig8_profiles.title: Figure 8. Segment means relative to all customers
fig8_profiles.caption: Profiles cover 5,839 customers and 3 groups including Outlier-Wholesale. Cells standardise raw segment means using the all-customer mean and standard deviation; the outlier label does not establish a wholesale business model.

cancellations_monthly.definition: Distinct identified-customer cancellation invoices divided by distinct identified-customer cancellation plus valid identified-customer gross purchase invoices; merchandise codes only. Same invoice ratio as the customer profiling feature.

features.cancellation_decision: Retained for profiling, excluded from clustering: zero inflation and limited log-transform change. AOV also profiles only: it is exactly Monetary divided by Frequency.

outliers.rule: Upper Tukey fence on log1p net customer Monetary; descriptive high-value group, not confirmed wholesale.

model.selection_rule: Choose the highest full-sample silhouette across feature sets and candidate k; exact ties use higher stability, lower Davies-Bouldin and lower k. Stability varies initialisation, not customers or time.
model.id_rule: Pipeline cluster centres reordered by mean raw net Monetary, descending.

model_test.origin: Synthetic combination of rounded non-outlier marginal medians; AOV recomputed exactly as Monetary/Frequency.

facts: No browsing events, marketing spend, margins, acquisition dates or return reasons supplied.
Observed cancellations are invoice events, not a complete physical-return rate.
Single UK retailer; historical window and incomplete final month limit generalisation.
Customer/product LIFO is an allocation assumption, not an invoice-linked return record; prices may differ.
Net sales retrospectively attribute matched returns to original purchase months; unmatched returns are not deducted from unrelated sales.
K-Means assumes Euclidean compact groups after transformation; clusters may overlap and are descriptive.
RFM is backward-looking; correlations and segment associations are not causal effects.
Outlier-Wholesale is a requested operational label; buyer type is not observed.
Initialisation stability is not temporal or resampling stability; there is no predictive holdout target.
Actions are hypotheses for controlled tests; no uplift or profit claims are made.
